description_full: Northeast Community Bancorp, Inc. operates as the holding company for NorthEast Community Bank that provides financial services for individuals and businesses. It accepts various deposit instruments, including checking accounts, money market accounts, regular savings accounts, and non-interest-bearing demand accounts, as well as certificates of deposits. The company also offers construction, commercial and industrial loans, multifamily and mixed-use real estate, non-residential real estate loans, and consumer loans. In addition, it invests in various types of liquid assets, including U.S. Treasury obligations, municipal securities, deposits at the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York, and certificates of deposit of federally insured institutions, as well as securities of various federal agencies, and state and municipal governments. Further, the company offers life insurance products and fixed rate annuities. It operates full-service branches located in Bronx, New York, Orange, Rockland, and Sullivan Counties in New York, Essex, Middlesex, and Norfolk Counties in Massachusetts; and loan production offices located in White Plains, New York; New City, New York; and Danvers, Massachusetts. Additionally, the company provides services such as personal loans and overdraft protection, and utilizes brokered, listing service, and military deposits, as well as borrowings, sources of funds, and retail deposit products. Northeast Community Bancorp, Inc. was founded in 1934 and is headquartered in White Plains, New York.

financial_summary: NorthEast Community Bancorp, In is a small-cap financial services business with a $401M market cap on $105M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +6.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 8% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $51M in free cash flow — roughly 48 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.18× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 13% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
